findings.passage: “Strong federal background checks and bans on rapid-fire devices are important tools for keeping communities safe and preventing mass shootings.”
findings.note: Attorney General's release on joining about a dozen states to defend two federal ATF actions: the nationwide ban on forced reset triggers and the 'engaged in the business' rule, which requires more sellers to be licensed and run background checks.
subjects: ban on rapid-fire devices (forced reset triggers)

findings.motion: Joined 15-state motion to defend ATF ban on forced reset triggers, and 14-state intervention to defend ATF 'engaged in the business' rule (background checks for more gun sellers)
findings.note: Maryland filed with other states in federal court to defend two ATF actions: the ban on forced reset triggers and the rule widening who must hold a dealer licence and run background checks.
subjects: ban on rapid-fire devices (forced reset triggers)

findings.passage: “While the Second Amendment affords Marylanders the right to bear arms, that right has never meant guns must be allowed everywhere, regardless of the wishes of business owners or their communities. But today’s ruling allows firearms into the restaurants, stores, and public spaces Marylanders visit every day unless owners take steps to keep the guns out. Marylanders are less safe when commonsense policies like this one are struck down. While we disagree with today's decision, keeping Marylanders safe remains my Office’s top priority.”
findings.note: Statement on the Supreme Court's 6-3 Wolford v. Lopez ruling against laws that bar carrying guns onto private property open to the public without the owner's consent; he disagrees with the ruling and says it makes Marylanders less safe.
subjects: Second Amendment and gun safety laws

findings.passage: I have long supported common-sense gun measures, and will continue to do so, that will prevent much of the violence that is plaguing our communities.
findings.note: Statement on the U.S. Surgeon General's advisory calling firearm violence a public health crisis; he calls gun violence an epidemic in Maryland and says he supports common-sense gun measures.
subjects: general statement on gun safety laws

findings.passage: The attorneys general argue that the rule is necessary to close a dangerous loophole and stop people who are banned from owning guns from sidestepping existing law—which they were able to do before gun kits were subject to the same regulations as other firearms.
findings.note: Release on his joining 24 attorneys general in a Supreme Court friend-of-the-court brief in Garland v. VanDerStok urging the Court to uphold the federal ghost gun rule (serial numbers and background checks for kits and part-built guns). This sentence describes the coalition's argument in a release issued by his office; he is not separately quoted.

findings.motion: Joined multistate amicus brief in Garland v. VanDerStok supporting federal ghost gun rule
findings.note: Maryland signed a 24-attorney-general brief asking the Supreme Court to reverse the Fifth Circuit and uphold the ATF rule treating gun kits and near-complete frames as firearms.

findings.passage: “Regulation by the federal government of the transfer of firearms across state lines supports and enhances states’ ability to protect their residents from gun violence,” explained Attorney General Brown. “Firearms that cross state lines, many of which are illegally trafficked, are more likely to be used in criminal activity. This is a commonsense measure that protects Marylanders.”
findings.note: Release on his joining 22 attorneys general in an amicus brief in U.S. v. Perez, defending the federal rule that out-of-state gun transfers go through a licensed dealer, and state dealer record-keeping rules.

findings.motion: Joined 22-AG amicus brief in U.S. v. Perez (Second Circuit) supporting federal limits on interstate firearm transfers and dealer regulation
findings.note: Maryland joined a coalition brief defending the federal ban on receiving out-of-state guns except through a licensed dealer.

findings.passage: “This is great news for Maryland and common-sense gun laws. This law helps prevent tragedies and keeps families safe, by keeping guns away from those who want to harm our communities,” said Attorney General Brown. “Thoughts and prayers are not enough – Maryland’s Handgun Qualification Licensing law is a key tool in our fight to end gun violence.”
findings.note: His statement, as reprinted by a regional news site, after the Supreme Court declined to hear a challenge to Maryland's handgun qualification licence (fingerprints, background check, training course).

findings.motion: Maryland Shall Issue v. Moore, Fourth Circuit (14-2), upholding handgun qualification licence; defended by the Attorney General's office, with his statement welcoming the ruling
findings.note: The same page reprints his 2024-08-23 statement after the full Fourth Circuit rejected a Second Amendment challenge to the handgun licence law; the Supreme Court declined review on 2025-01-13.
